claims.statement: The scheduler graph (agent/scheduler.py) is a single-node StateGraph (START -> launch -> END) registered as the `scheduler` assistant in langgraph.json; its `_launch` node deterministically selects one task handler without invoking an LLM, and boundedly retries transient sandbox-attach failures before returning `sandbox_unavailable`.

The scheduler's `_launch` routes `reconcile`, `baby_sit`, `background_tasks`, workspace refresh current/legacy task names, `session_cost`, `thread_feedback`, and `agent_cost` to dedicated handlers; legacy expedited-review ticks delete old crons, while an unrecognized task falls through to `launch_scheduled_agent_run(schedule_id)`.

When a scheduler tick is missing its required key (watch_key, thread_id, or schedule_id), `_launch` returns a `missing_*` status result instead of raising, so a malformed tick degrades to a no-op rather than crashing the cron.

Dashboard-managed recurring agent schedules validate cron strings with normalize_cron_schedule, which requires a five-field expression and range-checks each field (supporting steps, ranges, and lists) before a schedule is stored.

launch_scheduled_agent_run loads a stored schedule record and launches a fresh agent run, recording last_thread_id / last_run_id / last_triggered_at (or last_error) in a separate schedule run-state namespace.

reconcile_stale_runs is the durable-dispatch safety net: it paginates every `busy` thread, lists its `pending` runs, and cancels (action=interrupt) those older than max_age_seconds (default 1800s), so runs whose completion webhook never fired do not hold a thread busy forever.
The reconcile sweep wraps per-thread work in try/except so one bad thread never aborts the sweep, and returns counts of threads checked, stale runs found, and runs cancelled.

Session-cost refresh is a self-terminating chain of stateless delayed runs: completion schedules a `session_cost` run, and run_session_cost_refresh performs one Slack-footer update attempt, enqueuing the next attempt only for a transient `pending` result up to a fixed retry-delay list.

Each baby-sit watch is a BabySitWatch persisted in the `baby_sit_watches` store keyed by lower-cased owner/repo#pr_number, binding the watch to the originating agent thread_id, head SHA/ref, GitHub App installation id, captured run_config, and a SourceContext.

A pull request may be watched from only one agent thread at a time: start_watch rejects a second thread that tries to watch an already-active PR, and carries over retry/dedupe state only when the head SHA is unchanged.

start_watch registers each watch's per-watch LangGraph cron via _ensure_watch_cron, which idempotently reuses an existing cron tagged kind=baby_sit_watch (deleting duplicates) or creates one, and rolls back the store row and partial cron if cron creation fails for a brand-new watch.

The per-watch baby_sit cron fires on the fixed `*/10 * * * *` schedule against the scheduler assistant, providing a deterministic ten-minute fallback that dispatches no agent run for pending or duplicate CI state.

Signed GitHub CI webhooks trigger immediate watch evaluation: the webhook route verifies the X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC before processing, and handle_ci_webhook ignores incomplete/non-CI payloads, matches active watches by head SHA or branch, and de-duplicates by webhook delivery_id.

Both the webhook trigger and the cron trigger funnel into evaluation under a per-key short-lived lock thread, so at most one evaluation of a given watch runs at a time and concurrent triggers dispatch a failure only once.

On a new head SHA evaluation resets retry_count and failure/alert dedupe lists; on a new failing state it dispatches a `/baby-sit --continue` run to the originating agent thread, skips a previously dispatched per-head/retry fingerprint, and removes that fingerprint if dispatch fails.

Flaky reruns are capped per head SHA at MAX_RETRIES_PER_HEAD (3), and record_retry increments the durable retry count only for the owning thread and current head while posting the flaky-CI notification only once for a given head/check/safe GitHub URL via alert_keys dedupe.

Blocked checks, retry exhaustion, and MAX_EVALUATION_ERRORS consecutive evaluation failures finish a baby-sit watch by preferring its Slack or GitHub source destination, falling back to an enqueued `/baby-sit --terminal` run on the originating thread, and then stopping the watch; a closed PR simply stops without notification.

The manage_baby_sit tool is the agent-facing surface for durable watches: it validates canonical GitHub PR URLs, an executable thread, open-PR/head state, authentication and GitHub App installation on start, while stop and record_retry require ownership by the current thread.

background_tasks provides model-free monitoring: ensure_background_task_cron idempotently registers a kind=background_tasks cron on the every-minute (* * * * *) schedule bound to a thread, and monitor_background_tasks claims each terminal task atomically, dispatches a completion message to the originating thread, and deletes its own cron once no task is running or pending so monitoring self-terminates.

schedule_thread_wakeup schedules a one-shot re-trigger of the current agent thread (1 minute to 24 hours) as a single-fire cron against the `agent` assistant carrying an end_time ~90s past the fire so it never re-fires, and passes through selected config keys with a default polling prompt.

Thread wakeups are budget-limited to at most _MAX_WAKEUPS_BETWEEN_USER_MESSAGES (10) between human messages, keyed to the latest human-message generation so the budget resets on a new human message but not on system-kind messages.

Because a fired wakeup cron's row is never deleted by firing, schedule_thread_wakeup opportunistically purges expired thread_wakeup crons (matched conservatively on kind plus a past end_time) before creating a new one.

The baby-sit skill instructs cloud runs to use the durable manage_baby_sit watch (webhook + 10-minute token-free fallback) while local/desktop runs instead use a bounded foreground `gh pr checks --watch` loop and never call manage_baby_sit or schedule_thread_wakeup.

Agent-usage cost refresh uses the scheduler's `agent_cost` task to fetch a run-only LangSmith cost and persist it to the agent invocation usage record; unavailable or failed retrieval/persistence advances through the fixed five-delay retry budget and then terminates.

The purge_wakeup_crons operational script supports a dry run and deletion mode for expired `thread_wakeup` crons, resolving the deployment URL from `--url` or `LANGGRAPH_URL` and credentials from `LANGGRAPH_API_KEY` or `LANGSMITH_API_KEY`.

Focused tests cover baby-sit lifecycle, concurrency, failure and retry deduplication, green required-check completion, and head resets; they also cover wakeup validation, context, human-generation limits, concurrent limits, and expired-cron cleanup.

The `thread_feedback` scheduler task defers feedback until a matching agent thread is quiet and its latest run succeeded, re-enqueuing after the remaining five-minute quiet interval when the thread is busy.

Workspace refreshes have full and update modes: successful scripts are captured from a throwaway builder sandbox, while failures retain the previous snapshot; daily full crons are staggered by workspace slug and stale snapshot creation can start a one-shot update refresh.
